newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shares close lower on U.S. bond rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shares close lower on U.S. bond rate hike.

text.p: Brazil shares took a hit on Monday after a surge in U.S. long-bond yields pressured down Wall Street stock prices, brokers said.
"We did not expect such volatility in the U.S. markets. With little domestic news to look to, the local bolsas only had eyes to Wall Street today," a senior trader said.
The Bovespa index .BVSP of the 49 most traded stocks ended off 2.49 percent at 9.263 points. Market turnover was slightly lower than usual, totalling 538.7 million reais ($513.04 million).
The Dow Industrials was sharply lower before the market's close here.
Analysts said nervousness in the foreign exchange market also contributed to depress stock prices.

Earlier today the Central Bank set a new trading level for the real by buying dollars at 1.0591 per dollar and selling dollars at 1.0615, signalling a 0.28 percent depreciation if compared to the previous mini-band of between 1.0535 and 1.0585 reais per dollar which was set on March 11.

State mining giant Companhia Vale do Rio Doce (CVRD) fell 1.89 percent to 26 reais. State oil firm Petrobras lost 2.77 percent, closing at 210.50 reais.

Analysts said the market should rebound Tuesday as the Dow managed to end the day with a rise.
They noted, however, the market could suffer in the short-term if U.S. stock market remains volatile.
